page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7a.16xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance powered by the AMD EPYC 7T83 processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture and deployed via KVM virtualization, the instance supplies 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 32 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled at a base clock speed of 2.55 GHz. Memory configuration consists of 128.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining a 1:2 compute-optimized ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware security and instruction features include AES, VAES, and SHA-NI cryptographic acceleration alongside AVX instruction sets.

The instance does not bundle local NVMe or ephemeral storage, relying entirely on remote cloud block storage for persistent and temporary data volumes. Network interfaces provide a baseline network bandwidth of 16 Gbps. Hardware acceleration is absent, with zero GPUs included in the configuration.

Benchmark evaluations position the ecs.c7a.16xlarge in the top 25% for intensive compute tasks, reflected in its stress-ng multi-core metric of 86,349.63 and PassMark CPU score of 59,199.92. Memory-bound and integer workloads demonstrate high throughput, achieving 61.81 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations and 275.48 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. In contrast, uncached large-block memory operations and Geekbench composite scores place the instance in the middle 50% tier, showing 85.04 GB/sec read bandwidth on 256 MB blocks.

By delivering high parallel CPU density without the operational expense of attached local NVMe drives or discrete GPUs, the server provides balanced cost efficiency for core-heavy applications. The ecs.c7a.16xlarge is suited for multi-threaded batch compute, in-memory caching clusters, high-concurrency web microservices, and distributed data processing pipelines.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7a.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by a 2.55 GHz AMD EPYC 7T83 processor on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores, 128.0 GB of system memory, and a 16 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The instance features no integrated local storage and no hardware GPUs, routing all disk I/O through external cloud storage. Benchmark results show high performance across multi-threaded computational workloads, achieving top-quartile results in multi-core stress testing, encryption, and in-memory key-value processing with Redis reaching 61.81 million operations per second. Its 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio delivers cost-effective resource utilization for compute-intensive demands where high memory capacity is not strictly required. The instance is suited for multi-threaded data transformation, batch processing, application serving, and distributed caching clusters.
